common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acetaminophen Toxicity (overdose).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Other co-ingested substance without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any intentional overdose — needs psychiatric safety evaluation regardless of the medical outcome.
management_principles: Obtain a serum acetaminophen level at least 4 hours after a single acute ingestion, use the Rumack-Matthew nomogram when applicable, and start N-acetylcysteine promptly when indicated
Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: ingestion of 25 extra-strength Tylenol tablets 6 hours ago with mild nausea and normal initial AST/ALT

22F intentional overdose presenting 6 hours post-ingestion with serum acetaminophen level of 180 mcg/mL plotting above the Rumack-Matthew nomogram treatment line requiring immediate initiation of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) glutathione precursor to prevent acute liver failure.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination. Evaluate for pertinent signs.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Acetaminophen Toxicity Overdose Hepatotoxicity.
reference_soap.plan: Start N-acetylcysteine immediately because the 6-hour acetaminophen concentration plots above the Rumack-Matthew treatment line. Obtain baseline and serial liver tests, INR, renal function, glucose, and acid-base status; continue therapy according to the treatment protocol and laboratory response. Obtain toxicology/poison-center guidance and complete psychiatric safety assessment after medical stabilization because this was an intentional ingestion.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical features and diagnostic criteria of Acetaminophen Toxicity Overdose Hepatotoxicity
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for ingestion of 25 extra-strength Tylenol tablets 6 hours ago with mild nausea and normal initial AST/ALT
Select appropriate laboratory and imaging studies for emergency medicine
Implement evidence-based acute and long-term management strategies

teaching.one_liner: A large acetaminophen overdose depletes the liver's glutathione stores, and the resulting toxic metabolite causes delayed liver failure — the Rumack-Matthew nomogram determines whether N-acetylcysteine is needed, and it works best started early, before liver enzymes even rise.
differentials: Viral hepatitis (unrelated cause of elevated LFTs)
red_flags: Any intentional overdose — needs psychiatric safety evaluation regardless of the medical outcome

must_ask.say: How many tablets did you take, and exactly when?
Was this intentional, or an accident?
Did you take anything else along with the Tylenol, like alcohol or other pills?
Are you feeling nauseated, or any pain in your upper right belly?
Have you had thoughts of hurting yourself before, or are you having them now?

history.answer: I swallowed 25 extra-strength Tylenol pills about 6 hours ago, and I started feeling sick to my stomach.
I took them all at once at home around 6 hours ago, at about 6 o'clock this evening.
I took exactly 25 tablets from an extra-strength 500-milligram bottle, so it was about 12 and a half grams in total.
I was feeling overwhelmed and hopeless after a terrible personal argument, and I took them wishing I wouldn't wake up. I regret it now and got scared, which is why I came to the emergency room.
No, I didn't take any other medications, sleeping pills, aspirin, or illegal drugs with them.
No, I have not had any beer, wine, or liquor today at all.
The queasiness started gradually about two hours ago, and it feels like a persistent mild sick-feeling in my stomach.
It is just general nausea in my upper stomach area, not a sharp pain.
The nausea has stayed about the same since it began; it has not gotten much worse, but it has not gone away either.
Nothing makes it better, and thinking about eating or drinking anything makes the nausea slightly worse.
I have not thrown up, and I do not have diarrhea, sweats, or chills.
No, I have not had any fever, yellow eyes or yellow skin, dark tea-colored urine, unusual bruising, or confusion.
No, I have never taken an overdose or tried to harm myself before.
I tried drinking a small glass of water to settle my stomach, but I did not take anything else and did not make myself vomit.
I had a severe fight with my partner and felt like everything in my life was falling apart, which triggered an impulsive decision.
I have been having trouble focusing on my college classes and sleeping poorly for the past month because of stress, but I was functioning until tonight.

history.answer: I have felt down and anxious over the past several weeks, but I have never been officially diagnosed with depression or seen a psychiatrist.
I thought taking those over-the-counter pain pills wouldn't actually hurt me since I only feel slightly sick to my stomach.
I'm terrified that my parents will find out I tried to do this and force me to drop out of college.
I was hoping you could just give me something to settle my stomach and let me go home without calling my family.
I have always been healthy and do not have any chronic medical illnesses.
I have never had surgery and have never been admitted to a hospital before.
I do not take any daily prescription medications, birth control pills, herbal supplements, or vitamins.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used electronic vapes.
I only drink a glass of wine socially once or twice a month, and I have never had a problem with drinking.
I am a senior university student living in an off-campus apartment with a roommate.
My parents are alive and healthy, and there is no history of liver disease or early medical problems in my family.
My last menstrual period started about two weeks ago, and my menstrual cycles are always regular every 28 days.
I use condoms for protection, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.
